question.text: Which of the following is a key difference between open-ended and closed-ended mutual fund schemes?

answer.text: Open-ended schemes have a fixed maturity date while closed-ended don't
Closed-ended schemes allow continuous purchase and redemption at NAV
Open-ended schemes allow continuous investment and redemption at NAV, while closed-ended schemes issue units only during the NFO and the units are mandatorily listed on a stock exchange
Open-ended schemes must be listed on stock exchanges

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM-Series-X-A (p.203) describes open-ended schemes as allowing continuous NAV-based purchase and redemption transactions, while closed-ended schemes issue units only during the NFO, run for a fixed term, and have units mandatorily listed on a stock exchange. The Trap: The listing requirement applies to closed-ended schemes, not to open-ended schemes; reversing this is a common error. Note: The claim that closed-ended units routinely trade at a discount to NAV is not in the checked page and should be cited from a separate source before being asserted.
